name: txr
desc: Lisp-like programming language for convenient data munging
why: A Lisp-like language for data munging with pattern matching in both directions; an unusual, underknown corner worth an afternoon.

brief.what_it_is: TXR is a programming language with two parts: a whole-document pattern matching and extraction language for pulling information out of arbitrary text, and TXR Lisp, a general data-processing Lisp dialect. It takes text or structured data as input and produces extracted or transformed data as output. The homepage says many tasks can be done as one-liners from the shell prompt. It also includes an Awk implementation as a Lisp macro.
brief.why_it_exists: The author describes TXR as a convenient tool for daily hacking and data munging, aimed at messy, loosely structured text that is hard to handle with regexps or Awk-style field splitting. The project values brevity: programs should be short and clear.
brief.how_it_works: The pattern language uses nested, recursive pattern matching that binds variables, rather than imperative statements. Each construct ends by matching, failing, or throwing an exception, and searching and backtracking are implicit. TXR Lisp is a new dialect, not an implementation of Common Lisp or Scheme, and it compiles to a register-based virtual machine bytecode with an optimizing compiler.
brief.install_notes: Packaged by GNU Guix, NixOS, Chimera Linux, Alpine Linux, Void Linux, EasyBuild and T2. Binary downloads are available for several platforms, and 32-bit and 64-bit Windows installers exist for TXR 302. The source build needs only GNU Make, GCC or Clang, and a few shell utilities for configure. It has no external dependencies except libffi. The homepage explicitly says not to install it through Homebrew, so the suggested brew install should not be used.
brief.standout: Its pattern language matches whole documents with nested, recursive bindings instead of working line by line like Awk, and it still handles simple one-liners. The project is also small: the executable is about 1.7 MB, and peak memory when compiling its standard library is around 18 MB.
brief.status: Unknown from the homepage alone. The page is active and refers to TXR 302 and a Git repository, and says the project started in 2009, but it gives no release date or last-commit date. I did not fetch the release notes or repository to check.
brief.caveats: The homepage warns: 'Do not use TXR via Homebrew.' It says Homebrew packages contain an unstable, unreliable executable, that some users could not build the Homebrew formula, and that the formula does not run make tests. The project suspects Homebrew's compiler code generation flags. The Homebrew package is the one listed in the scout notes, so it should be avoided. The reference manual is very long, about 900 pages as a man-page-style PDF, so the learning curve is steep. The page itself says the language is 'no longer a small language'. The license is the two-clause BSD license.
quotes: TXR: an Original, New Programming Language for Convenient Data Munging
TXR is a pragmatic, convenient tool ready to take on your daily hacking challenges with its dual personality
